method: Full multi-agent protocol: fresh verifier sub-agent and fresh adversarial falsifier sub-agent run in parallel, neither having drafted the story. Both independently found and read Google's own blog post (which itself contains both the launch announcement and a same-page 31 July rollback update), Futurism's independent reporting including its own reproduced examples, and Forbes's account of Henk van Ess's demonstrations and the SynthID/Hive AI detection test. This cycle's orchestrating context then directly live-fetched blog.google and futurism.com and forbes.com itself to confirm the verifier/falsifier quotes before drafting. NPR (npr.org) was cited by both sub-agents for an equivalent Hive AI watermark-defeat test but two direct WebFetch attempts by this cycle timed out, so NPR was left out of the article's source list; Forbes's own statement of the same Hive AI figure was used instead and is live-fetch-confirmed. Falsifier specifically checked for: contradicting/denying reports (none found), whether this was a recycled story about the unrelated 2025 Gemini image-generation controversy (ruled out, distinct product and failure mode), product misidentification (confirmed as Google Earth, not Maps or Gemini app), single-source/wire-relay risk (partially present among smaller outlets, but Google's own statement plus Futurism's and Forbes's own reporting clear the independence bar), and hoax/satire/correction (none found). Falsifier flagged that the SynthID claim needed nuance (watermark was present but trivially defeated by screenshotting, not simply absent) -- reflected in the article's phrasing.
origin_items: Surfaced via this cycle's Tier-0 sweep of blog.google (checked as part of the broader lab/company sweep) and independently via the discovery/triage pass over quality-press coverage. dedup-check run before opening: no match against the archive.

claims.text: Google added an AI image-generation feature, powered by its Nano Banana 2 model, to the web version of Google Earth on 30 July 2026, letting users tap 'create image' after zooming to a location and type a prompt to generate imagery layered onto Google Earth's real satellite, aerial and 3D data
claims.reasoning: Directly confirmed by live-fetching Google's own blog.google announcement post.

claims.text: Google said generated images did not appear in the main Google Earth experience for other users to see and were watermarked as AI-generated using SynthID
claims.reasoning: Stated directly in the primary Google announcement, live-fetched.

claims.text: Within a day of launch, users demonstrated the tool could generate convincing fake imagery tied to real coordinates: Henk van Ess fabricated a nuclear facility in Iran and refugee scenes near the US-Mexico border, and Futurism independently reproduced the capability with its own generated images of a Pennsylvania town hit by drought and wildfire
claims.reasoning: Independently reproduced: Futurism ran its own separate tests distinct from Van Ess's examples (confirmed via direct live fetch of futurism.com), and Forbes independently reported Van Ess's demonstration (live-fetched). Two independent parties producing convincing fake imagery clears the capability-claim reproduction bar even though Van Ess's specific examples are cited by only one origin (himself, relayed by press).

claims.text: Google's SynthID watermark could be defeated simply by photographing or screen-recording a generated image; a screen recording tested with Hive AI's detector was rated only 1% likely to be AI-generated
claims.reasoning: Confirmed via direct live fetch of Forbes, which is the only outlet in this article's source list carrying this specific figure (NPR reportedly ran an equivalent test per both sub-agents' research but could not be live-fetched this cycle to confirm directly, so was not added as a second source).

claims.text: Google rolled back the image-generation feature on 31 July 2026, about a day after launch, citing screenshots of generated imagery that appear to violate its policies and stating it would work on 'stronger guardrails'
claims.reasoning: The rollback statement appears as a same-page update on Google's own primary announcement post, live-fetched directly; corroborated independently by Futurism and Forbes.
